blocks.text: 51 קְרוֹבוֹת לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 51
uncertainties: This is the running head with the page numbers, not prayer text.

blocks.text: פותחים הארון.
uncertainties: Small Rashi-script rubric, unpointed. In Rashi script ת looks like ח and א looks like ח, so a literal glyph-shape reading would be 'פוחחים החרון'. I read it as 'פותחים הארון'.

blocks.text: מִי כָמוֹךָ אַב הָרַחֲמִים. זוֹכֵר יְצוּרָיו לַחַיִּים בְּרַחֲמִים. וְנֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לְהַחֲיוֹת מֵתִים. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מְחַיֵּה הַמֵּתִים:
uncertainties: The vowel inside final kaf of כָמוֹךָ could be qamats or sheva; it is not clearly resolved.
Dagesh in the yod of לַחַיִּים is likely but faint.
וְנֶאֱמָן is printed with a heavy cluster of points; I read segol under nun and hataf-segol under alef.

blocks.text: סוגרים הארון.
uncertainties: Rashi-script rubric. The glyph shapes look like 'קונריס החרון'. I read it as 'סוגרים הארון' because Rashi-script samekh and gimel resemble qof and nun, and because it pairs with the opening-ark rubric above.

blocks.text: ע״ס א״ת ב״ש.
uncertainties: Probably expands to 'על סדר את-בש', i.e. the stanza is ordered as an atbash acrostic. The stanza confirms this: א ת ב ש ג ר ד ק ה צ ו פ ז ע ח ס ט נ י מ כ ל.

blocks.text: ק׳
uncertainties: Superscript siglum before אֶבֶן, probably קהל (congregation).

blocks.text: אֶבֶן חוּג מְצוּק נְשִׁיָּה. תְּהוֹם רַבָּה צוּל שְׁאִיָּה. בְּפִנַּת רֹאשׁ יְסוֹד שְׁלִישִׁיָּה. שֻׁתְּתוּ שְׁעוּן בָּהּ לְשִׁעְיָה. גִּבְעַת שֹׁרֶשׁ מְאוּסַת בּוֹנִים. רְבָעָה הַיּוֹם מֵאַרְבָּעָה אֲבָנִים. דְּמָעוֹת מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנִים. קָשְׁבָה מִנְעִי אֵם הַבָּנִים: הָאַדְמוֹן כְּבָט שֶׁלֹּא חָלָה. צָבָה לְקַחְתָּהּ לוֹ וְנִתְבֶּהָלָה. וּפִלְּלָה רַבִּים בְּעַד הַתּוֹחֵלָה. פְּדוּתָהּ מִזֵּד וְלֹא חֻלָּלָה. זָכַר לָהּ יֹשֶׁר אֳרָחוֹת. עוֹבֵר לְהָמִיר בְּבֶטֶן אָחוֹת. הֻשְׁבָה כְּהַיּוֹם זְכָרָהּ לְהֵאָחוֹת. סִלּוּף דִּינָה בִּיהוֹסֵף לְהַנְחוֹת: טֶבַע כִּכְלִי יוֹצֵר הֶעֱבִיר. נִסֵּי חֲיָלִים לְהַעֲצִים וּלְהַגְבִּיר. יָהּ כְּסָבְרַת אֶנְקַת גְּבִיר. מַטּוֹרַת שְׁנַיִם מֶנָּהּ הִסְבִּיר: כַּעֲקֶרֶת בַּיִת בְּתֶחֶל נְכָרָה. כִּבְכוֹר רֵאשִׁית בְּתֵבֶל בְּכָרָה.
uncertainties: שֻׁתְּתוּ: I read qubuts under shin and dagesh plus sheva in the first tav.
שְׁעוּן: the dot on the vav could be shuruq (וּ) or holam (וֹ).
לְשִׁעְיָה: the vowels on lamed, shin, ayin and yod are low-confidence, and I see no dagesh in the yod. The rhyme pattern (-יָּה) may call for לִשְׁעִיָּה, but I have not imposed it.
מְאוּסַת: a dagesh in the samekh is possible but not certain.
רְבָעָה: the vowel and dagesh on resh and bet are unclear; it could be רְבֻעָה or רִבְּעָה.
אֲבָנִים: the vowel under alef may be hataf-patah; read as printed.
מִנְעִי: hiriq under mem and sheva under nun, as I read them.
כְּבָט: low confidence on the bet vowel.
פְּדוּתָהּ: the second letter could be dalet or resh (פְּרוּתָהּ). Dalet fits the meaning and the English ('delivered').
חֻלָּלָה: qubuts under het.
זָכַר לָהּ: mappiq visible.
הֻשְׁבָה: the first letter could be he or het (חֻשְׁבָה), and the vowel under it is unclear.
זְכָרָהּ: mappiq likely but faint.
לְהֵאָחוֹת: the vowel under he is tsere or segol.
בִּיהוֹסֵף: plene spelling with he is clearly printed. Do not normalize it to בְּיוֹסֵף.
כְּסָבְרַת: the vowels under kaf, samekh and bet are uncertain; it could be כִּסְבַרַת or כְּסָבַרַת.
מַטּוֹרַת: patah under mem and dagesh in tet are uncertain.
בַּיִת: the first letter could be bet or kaf (כַּיִת). Bet is expected from Ps 113:9.
נְכָרָה: the vowels under nun and kaf are unclear; it could be נִכְּרָה or נֻכְּרָה.
כִּבְכוֹר: hiriq and dagesh on the first kaf as I read them.
בְּתֵבֶל: the vowel under tav could be tsere or segol.
בְּכָרָה: the vowels are uncertain; it could be בִּכְּרָה.

blocks.text: ח׳
uncertainties: Superscript siglum before לְבַדֶּיהָ, probably חזן (cantor).

blocks.text: לְבַדֶּיהָ תַּעֲמוֹד בְּיוֹם זְכִירָה. לְהִזָּכֵר לָמוֹ כְּמוֹ נִזְכָּרָה:
uncertainties: לְבַדֶּיהָ: the vowel under bet (patah or qamats) and the dagesh in dalet are uncertain.
This couplet continues the line that ends בְּכָרָה; I split it off only because the speaker siglum changes.

blocks.text: יִמְלֹךְ יְיָ לְעוֹלָם אֱלֹהַיִךְ צִיּוֹן לְדֹר וָדֹר הַלְלוּיָהּ:
uncertainties: The dot in the final he of הַלְלוּיָהּ (mappiq) is faint.
Printed as one word with no maqaf.
I see no Biblical cantillation.

blocks.text: וְאַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ יוֹשֵׁב תְּהִלּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵל נָא:
uncertainties: I see no Biblical cantillation.

blocks.text: 51 Morning Praye: of the New Year 51
uncertainties: 'Praye:' is printed literally; the 'r' is damaged or broken in the source. Proposed correction: 'Prayer'.

blocks.text: מי
Who is like Thee, Father of compassion, who remembers His creatures for life in compassion. And Thou art faithful to revive the dead. Blessed art Thou, O Lord who revives the dead.
uncertainties: The missing comma after 'O Lord' is literal.

blocks.text: אבן

The fortress of heaven, the foundation of the earth, the roaring waves of the deep flood, found their firm foundation through the first born son of the third mother (of our people). She, the root of our people, who lacked children and was today surrounded by her sister's four sons, shed tears for children; then she heard divine comfort as a mother of children. When the tawny one (Esau) saw that she did not bear children, he hoped to possess her, then was she terrified. Fervently she prayed that his hope would not be fulfilled, that she might be delivered from the arrogant man and not be defiled. The Lord remembered the integrity of her ways, transformed the child in her sister's womb; she was remembered today, for God recalled her sisterly affection and granted Joseph instead of Dinah. He changed nature as with a potter's tool, to show the wonders of His strength and might. The Lord noted the plea of the strong (Jacob) and let two tribes emerge from her. As the barren woman of the household she was regarded as a stranger, but in the end a first born stemmed from her. May she protect her children on the day of remembrance, that they may be remembered as she herself was remembered.
uncertainties: 'chil-/dren' is hyphenated across a line break in the source; I joined it as 'children'.
'remem-/bered' is also hyphenated across a line break; I joined it as 'remembered'.

blocks.text: ימלך
The Lord will rule for eternity, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation, Halleluyah.
ואתה
And Thou, Holy One, dwellest above the songs of praise of Israel, O God.

notes: s130: The scan has no horizontal rule, so I transcribed the whole page. The four bands overlap (for example, the בּוֹנִים... line repeats in bands 1 and 2, and the יִמְלֹךְ line in bands 3 and 4). I resolved them against the full page and included each line once.
The opening and closing ark rubrics are in small Rashi-style type. The atbash note ע״ס א״ת ב״ש is in small square type.

Stanza structure: one atbash-acrostic piyyut. The congregation (ק׳) recites from אֶבֶן up to בְּכָרָה, and the cantor (ח׳) recites the closing couplet לְבַדֶּיהָ... נִזְכָּרָה:. The sof-pasuq colons divide it into quatrains: נְשִׁיָּה–לְשִׁעְיָה, גִּבְעַת–הַבָּנִים, הָאַדְמוֹן–חֻלָּלָה, זָכַר–לְהַנְחוֹת, טֶבַע–הִסְבִּיר, then כַּעֲקֶרֶת–נִזְכָּרָה.
No recitation role is printed for the יִמְלֹךְ and וְאַתָּה verses.
No printed conditional alternatives on these pages.
No citation references are printed. For identification only: יִמְלֹךְ = Ps 146:10; וְאַתָּה קָדוֹשׁ יוֹשֵׁב תְּהִלּוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל = Ps 22:4, with the added liturgical אֵל נָא.
s130 has no visible cantillation. Pointing in the piyyut is dense and the print is somewhat blurred; I flagged low-confidence vowels for each block rather than guessing.
The English translation (s131) omits the ark rubrics, the atbash note and the ק׳/ח׳ sigla. Every Hebrew prayer block has an English counterpart, so no passage is missing from the English.

Proposed corrections (source left as printed): s131 header 'Praye:' → 'Prayer'. On s130, no confirmed typos; the ambiguous readings above (פְּדוּתָהּ/פְּרוּתָהּ, בַּיִת/כַּיִת, הֻשְׁבָה/חֻשְׁבָה) need checking against a higher-resolution scan.
